sources.design: RCT,n=39; unblinded researcher; supervised multicomponent protocols.
sources.population: Young adults with CAI, questionnaire score≥11.
sources.comparator: Balance versus strength versus20 minmild cycling control.
sources.coInterventions: Strength included therapist manual PNF; no isolated component effects.
sources.outcomes: Both active arms improved balance/strength/side-hop at6 weeks; strength also improved eccentric eversion.
sources.uncertainty: Small sample; whole-program effects cannot be assigned to isolated stance/band exercise.
sources.harms: One participant excluded because unable to progress balance; systematic harms result not established.
sources.limitations: Small sample; whole-program effects cannot be assigned to isolated stance/band exercise. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Band DF/inversion/eversion seated on floor anchored around treatment table, band at metatarsal heads; heel raises on step with rail for balance; manual PNF. Balance progressive single-leg stance/open-closed eyes/hop-stabilisation/reach.
protocol.dose: Twenty-minute sessions. Band exercises: 3 × 10 and 4 × 10 on alternating weeks with increased resistance each fortnight. PNF and heel raises: 2 × 10 to 4 × 15. Band movement approximately 3–5 seconds per repetition.
protocol.frequency: Three times weekly for six weeks.
protocol.progression: Balance only after error-free prior level; strength weekly sets/resistance schedule.
protocol.stoppingRules: Balance progression required no touchdown, excessive trunk motion (trial defined >30 degrees), hand-position/bracing errors or missed target. These are progression criteria, not general contraindications.
